title: Letters Instead of Digits

concept.title: Give each letter a different digit, then check the sum
body: In a *cryptarithm* the digits of a sum are replaced by letters: the same letter always stands for the same digit and different letters for different digits. For example `ab + ba = cc` is true for `a = 1, b = 2, c = 3` (12 + 21 = 33). A number does not start with a zero, so the first letter of a word with more than one letter cannot be 0.

The search assigns a digit to the letters one by one, in order of first appearance, with a table `used` for the digits that are taken. A digit is skipped if it is taken, or if it is 0 and the letter is a leading letter. When every letter has a digit, the sum is checked.

With `L` letters there are at most `10 * 9 * ... * (10 - L + 1)` assignments, 151200 for six letters, which is why the number of different letters is limited. Smarter solutions check the sum column by column from the right and cut many assignments early, but even this plain version is fast enough here.

statement: You are given three words `a`, `b` and `c` of lowercase letters. Replace every letter by a digit: the same letter by the same digit and different letters by different digits. A word with more than one letter must not start with the digit 0. Count the replacements for which `a + b = c` is a true sum of numbers.
inputFormat: The only line has the three words.
constraints: There are at most 6 different letters in the three words together.

examples.note: a + b = c with a, b, c different, and a, b not 0: for example 12 + 21 = 33. There are 32 such replacements.

hints: List the different letters in order of first appearance and give them digits one by one.
A digit that is already used for another letter is not allowed.
A first letter of a longer word cannot be 0; check the sum when all letters have a digit.

explanation: Letters get distinct digits in order of first appearance (never 0 for a leading letter of a longer word). When all letters are assigned, the two sides of the sum are computed and compared.
solution.complexity: Time O(10!/(10-L)! * length) for L letters, at most 151200 assignments here.
